pop-rocks.blurb: Carbonated candy crystals that crackle and jump on your tongue, around since 1976

jianlibao.name: Jianlibao (健力宝)
jianlibao.blurb: China's 1984 orange-honey sports soda, nicknamed "Oriental magic water"

beibingyang.name: Beibingyang (北冰洋) soda
beibingyang.blurb: Beijing's polar-bear orange soda in glass bottles, gone in the late 1990s, back in 2011

xiaohuanxiong.name: Xiaohuanxiong (小浣熊) noodles

mailisu.name: Mailisu (麦丽素)

guodanpi.name: Guodanpi (果丹皮)

contra.name: Contra (魂斗罗)

game-boy.blurb: Nintendo's 1989 handheld with a green-tinted screen, four AA batteries and Tetris

tamagotchi.name: Tamagotchi

arcade.name: Arcade (游戏厅)

walkman.name: Walkman

xiaolingtong.name: Xiaolingtong (小灵通)

wenquxing.name: Wenquxing (文曲星)

yanghua.name: Yanghua (拍洋画)

xiaomaibu.name: Xiaomaibu (小卖部)
xiaomaibu.blurb: The tiny corner shop by the school gate where Chinese kids spent their pocket money
